author: ai
text: The OECD replaced the Organisation for European Economic Co-operation in 1961, with 19 members. Italy (1962), Japan (1964), Finland (1969), Australia (1971) and New Zealand (1973) joined next. Mexico (1994), Czechia (1995), Hungary, Poland and South Korea (all 1996) and Slovakia (2000) followed. Chile, Slovenia, Israel and Estonia joined in 2010, then Latvia (2016), Lithuania (2018), Colombia (2020) and Costa Rica (2021). The OECD had 38 members in 2026, and the facts list no departures or suspensions.
